- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.05) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3%.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast 3–5 days after spike at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.10) over 5+ days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast mean to counteract downward bias.
- Model frequently underestimates true mean in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; adjust downward bias by 0.5–1.0% of 30d mean.
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope by 0.1–0.3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model tends to lag in 30d forecasts when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for delayed reaction to sentiment shifts.
